# Implementation Plan: Full-Stack VendorEval Platform

**Branch**: `002-fullstack-platform` | **Date**: 2025-10-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-fullstack-platform/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command with Context7-verified architecture for all major libraries.

**UPDATE (2025-10-21)**: Added CMS Architecture section and updated deployment strategy to reflect two separate Vercel projects (docs site with custom CMS + evaluation tool). See "CMS Architecture (Documentation Site)" section for details.

## Summary

Transform VendorEval from a client-side LocalStorage application to a full-stack platform with Discord OAuth authentication (server membership verification), admin CMS for content management, dual-tone content system (No BS ↔ Corporate Friendly), and database-backed user evaluations. All existing content will be migrated from code to Supabase PostgreSQL database with auto-generated corporate versions using Claude API.

**Technical Approach**:
- **Backend**: Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth + Edge Functions) for all backend services
- **Frontend**: React 19 + Vite 7 + Tailwind CSS v4, deployed on Vercel
- **Authentication**: Discord OAuth 2.0 via Supabase Auth provider, membership verification via Discord API
- **Testing**: Vitest (unit/integration), Playwright (E2E), test after each feature area
- **Migration**: Seed script to populate database, Claude API to generate corporate tone versions

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.9+ (strict mode), Node.js 20+ (for scripts), Deno (for Edge Functions)
**Primary Dependencies**:
- Frontend: React 19, Vite 7, Tailwind CSS v4, @supabase/supabase-js, lucide-react
- Backend: Supabase Edge Functions (Deno runtime), Discord.js (for bot setup)
- Testing: Vitest, @testing-library/react, Playwright
- APIs: Anthropic Claude (tone generation), GitHub API (feedback issues), Discord API (membership check)

**Storage**: Supabase PostgreSQL with Row Level Security (RLS), dual-tone columns for all text content (_no_bs, _corporate)

**Testing**:
- Unit: Vitest with React Testing Library for components and utilities
- Integration: Vitest for auth flows, CMS operations, dual-tone system
- E2E: Playwright for complete user journeys (login → evaluate → export)
- Test after each feature area (Option B testing cadence)

**Target Platform**: Web (desktop + mobile responsive), browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari (latest 2 versions)

**Project Type**: Web application (monorepo with multiple apps: evaluation-tool, docs)

**Performance Goals**:
- Initial page load: < 3 seconds on 3G
- Tone toggle: < 500ms perceived lag
- Discord membership check: < 5 seconds
- Admin content edit → user-facing update: < 5 seconds
- Support 100 concurrent authenticated users

**Constraints**:
- No LocalStorage for evaluation data (must persist to database)
- All text content must have dual-tone versions (database columns)
- Discord server membership required (or invite code for exceptions)
- Super admin cannot be demoted (data constraint)
- Free tier budget: Supabase (500MB DB, 50K MAU), Vercel (100GB bandwidth)

**Scale/Scope**:
- ~100 Phase I users (Discord community members)
- 20 questions, 6 categories, 11 key entities
- 53 functional requirements
- ~50-60 medium-grained implementation tasks
- 8-week implementation timeline with AI assistance

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Article I: Code Quality Standards ✅

**TypeScript Strict Mode**: All application code (frontend + Edge Functions) will use TypeScript 5.9+ with strict mode.
- Frontend: React 19 with TypeScript
- Edge Functions: Deno runtime (TypeScript native)
- No `any` types except for @supabase/supabase-js client initialization

**Code Organization**: Component-based architecture maintained, max 300 lines per file.
- React components follow existing pattern
- Edge Functions: One function per file in `supabase/functions/`
- No circular dependencies enforced via ESLint

**Linting**: ESLint + Prettier configuration already in place from Phase I work.

### Article II: Testing Standards ✅

**Test Coverage**: 70% minimum for business logic (auth flows, evaluation state, CMS operations, tone conversion).

**Test Types**:
- Unit: Vitest for utility functions (scoring, data transformations, tone toggle)
- Component: React Testing Library for UI components
- Integration: Vitest for auth flows, CMS operations, dual-tone system
- E2E: Playwright for critical user journeys (login → evaluate → export)

**Test Cadence**: Test after each feature area (Option B from spec).

**TDD Encouraged**: Write tests before implementation for complex business logic.

### Article III: User Experience Standards ✅

**Design Principles**: Professional polish maintained for C-level executives.
- Current UI already meets this standard (Phase I validation complete)
- Admin CMS will match existing design system

**Accessibility**: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance required.
- Contrast ratios: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text
- Keyboard navigation for all admin CMS operations
- Screen reader compatible (semantic HTML, ARIA labels)
- Visible focus indicators on all interactive elements

**Loading/Error States**:
- Loading indicators for Discord membership check (< 5s)
- User-friendly error messages (no technical jargon)
- Confirmation dialogs for destructive admin actions (delete user, delete vendor)

**Note**: Database-backed system requires new loading states for async operations.

### Article IV: Performance Requirements ⚠️ ADAPTATION REQUIRED

**Load Time Targets**:
- Initial page load: < 3 seconds on 3G ✅ (maintained from Phase I)
- Route transitions: < 100ms (constitution) vs < 500ms (spec for tone toggle) → **Spec is looser, use 500ms**
- Tone toggle: < 500ms perceived lag ✅
- Discord membership check: < 5 seconds ✅ (new requirement)
- Admin content edit → user-facing update: < 5 seconds ✅ (new requirement)

**Bundle Size Limits**: Constitution limits still apply.
- Total JavaScript: < 500KB gzipped (verify after adding @supabase/supabase-js)
- Individual route chunks: < 150KB gzipped
- Admin CMS lazy-loaded (not in main bundle)

**Optimization Strategies**:
- Code splitting: Admin CMS behind lazy-loaded route
- Lazy load jsPDF (already implemented in Phase I)
- Debounce database writes (500ms idle, same as LocalStorage)
- Memoize category scoring (already implemented)

**Adaptation**: Database operations introduce network latency. Use optimistic UI updates where possible.

### Article V: Security and Privacy Standards ⚠️ MAJOR ADAPTATION

**Data Handling**: Constitution says "NO sensitive data leaves the browser (all storage is LocalStorage)".

**Adaptation Required**: This feature REQUIRES database persistence. Updated security model:
- User authentication data: Discord OAuth via Supabase (leaves browser)
- Evaluation data: Persisted to Supabase PostgreSQL (leaves browser)
- Notes: User-controlled, stored in database with RLS policies
- Export formats: NO tracking metadata (maintained)

**Privacy Measures**:
- Row Level Security (RLS) enforces user data isolation
- Admin users can only access their own evaluations (not other users' data)
- Discord membership checks happen server-side (Edge Function)
- NO analytics or tracking (maintained)
- Anonymize evaluations on user deletion (don't cascade delete)

**Input Validation**:
- Sanitize all admin CMS input (prevent XSS)
- Validate evaluation data structure before database insert
- Maximum note length: 5000 characters (enforced client + server)

**Dependency Security**:
- `npm audit` before adding Supabase client library
- Keep @supabase/supabase-js updated (security patches within 7 days)

**Constitutional Exception Documented**: Database persistence required for multi-user platform. Trade-off: Data leaves browser BUT protected by RLS, encryption at rest, and no third-party access.

### Article VI: Dependency Management ✅

**New Dependencies Required**:
1. **@supabase/supabase-js** (v2.x)
   - Active: Updated monthly
   - Community: 50K+ weekly downloads
   - License: MIT ✅
   - Bundle: ~50KB gzipped (acceptable)
   - Security: No known vulnerabilities

2. **discord.js** (bot setup only, dev dependency)
   - Used for initial Discord bot setup (one-time script)
   - Not included in production bundle

3. **@anthropic-ai/sdk** (admin CMS only, server-side)
   - Used in Edge Function for tone generation
   - Not included in frontend bundle

**All dependencies meet constitutional criteria.**

### Article VII: Error Handling and Logging ✅

**Error Handling Patterns**: All database operations wrapped in try/catch.
- Supabase errors translated to user-friendly messages
- Optimistic UI updates with rollback on failure
- Toast notifications for async operation results

**Logging Standards**:
- Development: Console logs allowed
- Production: Remove `console.log`, keep `console.error`
- Never log: User evaluation data, notes, Discord IDs

**Error Boundaries**: Wrap admin CMS in React ErrorBoundary (preserve user data).

### Article VIII: Content Standards ✅

**Dual Voice Mode**: ALL content available in both modes.
- Database columns: `field_no_bs`, `field_corporate` for ALL text fields
- Questions, categories, help text, vendor analyses, documentation → dual-tone required
- Translation Rule: Preserve meaning when switching modes

**Content Quality**: 20 questions match documented framework (already validated in Phase I).

**Content Migration**: Seed script populates database from existing code, Claude API auto-generates corporate versions.

### Article IX: Documentation Requirements ✅

**Required Documentation**:
- README.md: Update with Supabase setup, environment variables, deployment
- Edge Functions: JSDoc comments for authentication logic, membership checks
- Database Schema: Document RLS policies in data-model.md
- API Contracts: Document in contracts/ directory

**Architecture Decisions**: Document Discord OAuth flow, dual-tone database architecture, RLS policy design.

## CMS Architecture (Documentation Site)

### Overview

The documentation site uses a **custom React-based admin panel** integrated into Docusaurus, backed by the `pages` table in Supabase. This approach provides full control over the dual-tone editing experience while maintaining Docusaurus for public-facing content delivery.

### Why Custom CMS (vs Headless CMS)

**Requirements that drove this decision**:
- FR-030: Admins must CRUD documentation pages with Markdown editor
- FR-033: Side-by-side editors for "No BS" and "Corporate" versions
- FR-034: Auto-generate corporate version from no-bs using Claude API
- Need for frequent content changes (user requirement: comprehensive CMS)

**Custom CMS advantages**:
1. Full control over dual-tone split-pane editing experience
2. Native integration with existing Supabase setup (same database both apps use)
3. Direct integration with Claude API for tone generation
4. Consistent tech stack (React + TypeScript across all apps)
5. No additional services or dependencies to manage

**Rejected alternatives**:
- Static Docusaurus: Cannot meet "frequent changes" requirement
- Headless CMS (Strapi/Payload): Harder to implement dual-tone side-by-side editing, adds service complexity

### CMS Components

**Admin Panel** (`apps/docs/src/components/admin/`):

1. **PageEditor.tsx** - Main editing interface
   - Split-pane Markdown editor (Monaco Editor or similar)
   - Left pane: "No BS" version
   - Right pane: "Corporate" version
   - Live preview below each editor
   - "Auto-Generate Corporate" button (calls Claude API)
   - Save/Publish/Unpublish actions

2. **PageList.tsx** - Page management dashboard
   - List all pages with title, slug, published status
   - Search and filter capabilities
   - Create new page button
   - Edit/Delete actions

3. **ToneGenerator.tsx** - Claude API integration component
   - Takes "No BS" markdown content
   - Calls Claude API via Edge Function
   - Returns "Corporate" version
   - Allows manual editing after generation

4. **MarkdownPreview.tsx** - Live preview
   - Renders Markdown to HTML in real-time
   - Shows exactly how content will appear to users
   - Respects Docusaurus styling

**Database Integration** (`apps/docs/src/services/cms.ts`):

```typescript
// CMS service functions
export const cmsService = {
  // Fetch all pages (admin view)
  async getAllPages(): Promise<Page[]>

  // Fetch single page by slug
  async getPageBySlug(slug: string): Promise<Page>

  // Create new page
  async createPage(data: CreatePageInput): Promise<Page>

  // Update existing page
  async updatePage(id: string, data: UpdatePageInput): Promise<Page>

  // Delete page
  async deletePage(id: string): Promise<void>

  // Publish/unpublish page
  async togglePublishStatus(id: string, published: boolean): Promise<Page>

  // Auto-generate corporate version
  async generateCorporateTone(noBsContent: string): Promise<string>
}
```

**Docusaurus Plugin** (`apps/docs/src/plugins/database-content/`):

Purpose: Fetch published pages from Supabase and inject into Docusaurus routing system.

```javascript
// Plugin architecture
module.exports = function databaseContentPlugin(context, options) {
  return {
    name: 'database-content-plugin',

    async loadContent() {
      // Fetch published pages from Supabase
      const pages = await fetchPublishedPages();
      return pages;
    },

    async contentLoaded({content, actions}) {
      const {addRoute} = actions;

      // Create route for each page
      content.forEach(page => {
        addRoute({
          path: `/docs/${page.slug}`,
          component: '@site/src/components/DatabasePage.tsx',
          exact: true,
          metadata: page
        });
      });
    }
  };
};
```

### Content Flow

**Admin creates/edits content**:
1. Admin logs in to `/admin` (Supabase auth check)
2. Navigate to Pages section
3. Click "Create New Page" or "Edit" existing page
4. PageEditor component loads with split-pane Markdown editors
5. Admin writes "No BS" version in left pane
6. Click "Auto-Generate Corporate" button
7. ToneGenerator calls Claude API via Edge Function
8. Corporate version appears in right pane (editable)
9. Admin reviews both versions, makes adjustments
10. Click "Publish" → `is_published = true` in database

**User views content**:
1. User visits `/docs/{slug}`
2. Docusaurus plugin fetches page from Supabase (cached)
3. DatabasePage component renders content based on tone toggle
4. User can toggle between "No BS" and "Corporate" versions
5. Content updates instantly (no page reload)

### Edge Function: generate-corporate-tone

**Purpose**: Generate corporate version from no-bs content using Claude API.

**Location**: `supabase/functions/generate-corporate-tone/index.ts`

**Flow**:
```typescript
// Edge Function handler
export default async (req: Request) => {
  // 1. Verify admin authentication
  const user = await verifyAdminAuth(req);

  // 2. Extract no-bs content from request
  const { noBsContent } = await req.json();

  // 3. Call Claude API
  const client = new Anthropic({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });
  const response = await client.messages.create({
    model: 'claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022',
    max_tokens: 4096,
    system: TONE_CONVERSION_PROMPT,
    messages: [{
      role: 'user',
      content: noBsContent
    }]
  });

  // 4. Return corporate version
  return new Response(
    JSON.stringify({ corporateContent: response.content[0].text }),
    { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  );
};
```

**Tone Conversion Prompt**:
```
You are a professional tone translator. Convert the following "No BS" documentation content into a "Corporate Friendly" version.

Rules:
1. Preserve all technical meaning and accuracy
2. Replace informal language with professional equivalents
3. Soften direct/blunt statements while maintaining honesty
4. Keep structure and formatting (Markdown) identical
5. Maintain all links, code examples, and technical details

Example transformations:
- "This is broken and won't work" → "This approach has known limitations"
- "Don't be an idiot" → "Please exercise caution"
- "Magic black box" → "Proprietary system with limited transparency"

Convert the following content:
```

### Database Schema (Already Exists)

The `pages` table is already defined in [data-model.md](data-model.md) (lines 568-610):

```sql
CREATE TABLE pages (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  slug TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,

  -- Dual-tone content
  title_no_bs TEXT NOT NULL,
  title_corporate TEXT NOT NULL,
  content_no_bs TEXT NOT NULL,  -- Markdown
  content_corporate TEXT NOT NULL,

  is_published BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW() NOT NULL,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW() NOT NULL
);
```

**Migration**: Already planned as part of database setup (no changes needed).

### Performance Considerations

**Caching Strategy**:
- Published pages cached at build time (Docusaurus static generation)
- Admin edits trigger cache invalidation
- Use Vercel ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) for dynamic updates

**Bundle Size**:
- Admin panel lazy-loaded (not in public bundle)
- Monaco Editor loaded only when admin accesses PageEditor
- Claude API calls server-side only (no client bundle impact)

**Optimization**:
- Debounce auto-save in PageEditor (500ms idle)
- Markdown preview debounced (200ms)
- Optimistic UI updates for publish/unpublish actions

## Complexity Tracking

*Constitutional exceptions and complexity justifications documented here.*

| Exception/Complexity | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|-----------|------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Article V: Data leaves browser** | Multi-user platform requires database persistence, authentication, and content management. Cannot use LocalStorage for shared content and user accounts. | Client-side only storage (LocalStorage) insufficient for: (1) Multi-user access control, (2) Admin CMS content updates visible to all users, (3) Discord membership verification, (4) Vendor library shared across users. |
| **Article IV: 500ms tone toggle (vs 100ms route transition)** | Database query for dual-tone content introduces network latency. Spec allows 500ms, which is acceptable for this operation. | In-memory caching could reduce to ~100ms, but adds complexity (cache invalidation when admin edits content). 500ms provides acceptable UX while keeping implementation simple. |
| **6 database migrations** | Incremental deployment allows testing each feature area independently (core schema → vendors → evaluations → admin → feedback → RLS). | Single migration possible, but high-risk (no rollback points, harder to test). Incremental approach aligns with "test after each feature area" requirement. |
| **3 Edge Functions** | Discord membership checks, feedback submission, and tone generation require server-side execution (API keys, GitHub integration). | Client-side Discord API calls expose API keys. GitHub issue creation requires server-side token. Claude API for tone generation must be server-side (expensive API, rate limiting). |
| **Two Vercel Projects** | Documentation site requires custom CMS for frequent content changes (FR-030). Separating docs and evaluation tool allows independent deployment and clearer separation of concerns. | Single unified deployment initially attempted, but caused confusion with auto-created projects. Two projects simplifies: (1) Independent scaling, (2) Clear separation between content management (docs) and evaluation tool, (3) Different deployment cadences (docs change frequently, tool less so). |
| **Custom CMS vs Headless CMS** | Custom React admin panel provides full control over dual-tone split-pane editing (FR-033), native Supabase integration, and direct Claude API integration (FR-034). | Headless CMS (Strapi/Payload) rejected because: (1) Harder to implement side-by-side dual-tone editing, (2) Adds another service to manage, (3) Less control over UX, (4) More complex to integrate with Claude API for auto-generation. Custom CMS keeps tech stack consistent (React + TypeScript + Supabase). |

**Complexity Justification Summary**:

All complexity additions are **necessary** for Phase I requirements. No alternative architectures provide the required functionality without equal or greater complexity:

- Database persistence: Required for FR-001 (authentication), FR-015 (admin content management), FR-033 (vendor library)
- Edge Functions: Required for FR-003 (membership verification), FR-049 (feedback system), FR-023 (auto-generate corporate tone)
- Dual-tone database columns: Required for FR-015 (dual-tone content) and Article VIII (content standards)

**Trade-offs Accepted**:
- Data leaves browser → BUT protected by RLS, encryption at rest, no third-party access
- Network latency for tone toggle → BUT 500ms is within acceptable UX threshold
- Multiple migrations → BUT enables incremental testing and rollback
- Edge Functions → BUT avoids exposing API keys client-side

**No violations of constitutional principles** - only necessary adaptations for multi-user platform requirements.
